Every worker receives exactly the same reference before its own short question. These records are fictional and contain no operational instructions for the runtime. Record 01 planning: A planner lists measurable goals, assigns an owner to each goal, and writes a dependency map before any worker starts. Record 02 planning: A planner checks that each dependency has a named producer, a named consumer, and a stable output format. Record 03 planning: A planner estimates time from concrete subtasks, records uncertainty, and reserves time for independent review. Record 04 planning: A planner changes the schedule only after documenting which input assumption changed and who confirmed it. Record 05 planning: A planner reports incomplete work with a reason and a next action rather than silently treating it as complete. Record 06 verification: A reviewer compares each claim with a saved artifact and writes down the artifact identifier. Record 07 verification: A reviewer recomputes one representative numerical result independently and checks units and rounding. Record 08 verification: A reviewer checks that all required inputs were actually used and that missing values remain explicit. Record 09 verification: A reviewer records a mismatch as an observation, then asks for a corrected artifact or explanation. Record 10 verification: A reviewer distinguishes a successful software run from a correct scientific conclusion. Record 11 storage: A workspace keeps intermediate files under one run identifier so later reviews can reconstruct the sequence. Record 12 storage: A manifest records software versions, parameters, input hashes, and the start time for each run. Record 13 storage: A durable archive keeps raw responses alongside derived tables so calculations can be checked again. Record 14 storage: A file path is normalized before access, and a task cannot write outside its assigned workspace. Record 15 storage: A result table names each column and retains unknown values instead of replacing them with zeros. Record 16 scheduling: A coordinator sends independent tasks in a documented order and waits for each completion. Record 17 scheduling: A coordinator can run a serial baseline before testing a concurrent schedule with the same task set. Record 18 scheduling: A coordinator records a timeout separately from a model refusal, a tool error, or a missing response. Record 19 scheduling: A coordinator limits retries so one failing worker cannot consume an unbounded request budget. Record 20 scheduling: A coordinator gives every worker the same reference version when comparing their measured behavior. Record 21 measurement: A token report includes prompt, completion, total, cached, and uncached counts when available. Record 22 measurement: A cache hit is measured from server telemetry; similar text alone is insufficient evidence of reuse. Record 23 measurement: A prompt comparison uses exact token identifiers and a longest common prefix calculation. Record 24 measurement: A benchmark records warmup, cache namespace, server instance, and memory pressure as conditions. Record 25 measurement: An absent telemetry field is marked unknown because absence does not prove a zero count. Synthetic reference for a shared-prefix cache experiment.
